batch: OLP-0198–0202 Interpolation under the cumulative Model Theory profile
method: Fresh comparison of every exact frozen-English and Gujarati linguistic block, with independently worded reverse paraphrases for every substantive block. The review covers separation, the maximal inseparable-pair proof of Craig interpolation, explicit and implicit definability, Beth's theorem and all ten adjacent disclosed source repairs. Four rejected correction candidates were separately recorded and preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If A entails B, there is a sentence C such that A entails C and C entails B, and every nonidentity constant, function and predicate in C occurs in both A and B. Such a C is their interpolant.
samples.assessment: The introduction preserves the entailment conditions for an interpolant, its restriction to vocabulary shared by A and B, and the Beth definability and Robinson joint-consistency applications.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Beyond its intrinsic interest, interpolation proves results about definability and about when combining two consistent theories preserves consistency; these are Beth's and Robinson's theorems.
samples.assessment: The introduction preserves the entailment conditions for an interpolant, its restriction to vocabulary shared by A and B, and the Beth definability and Robinson joint-consistency applications.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An interpolant C for A and B is equivalently a sentence separating A from not-B, because C entails B exactly when not-B entails not-C. The proof therefore generalizes separation from two sentences to two sets of sentences.
samples.assessment: The section preserves separation as the contraposed form of interpolation, inseparability, the model-class diagram and both fresh-constant lemmas. OLINT-001 restores H in the contraposition argument and OLINT-002 restores the existential macro's scope.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: C separates Gamma and Delta exactly when Gamma entails C and Delta entails not-C; if no such sentence exists, the two sets are inseparable.
samples.assessment: The section preserves separation as the contraposed form of interpolation, inseparability, the model-class diagram and both fresh-constant lemmas. OLINT-001 restores H in the contraposition argument and OLINT-002 restores the existential macro's scope.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The diagram places every Gamma-model inside the C region and every Delta-model inside the not-C region, visually expressing the two entailments in the definition of separation.
samples.assessment: The section preserves separation as the contraposed form of interpolation, inseparability, the model-class diagram and both fresh-constant lemmas. OLINT-001 restores H in the contraposition argument and OLINT-002 restores the existential macro's scope.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If the common language contains precisely the nonidentity symbols shared by Gamma and Delta, adjoining infinitely many fresh constants does not make an inseparable pair separable.
samples.assessment: The section preserves separation as the contraposed form of interpolation, inseparability, the model-class diagram and both fresh-constant lemmas. OLINT-001 restores H in the contraposition argument and OLINT-002 restores the existential macro's scope.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Assuming a separator that uses a fresh constant, compactness reduces both entailments to finite conjunctions. Generalization removes that constant and contraposition yields a common-language universal sentence separating the original sets. The repaired conclusion is not-H, the consequent required by the preceding entailment.
samples.assessment: The section preserves separation as the contraposed form of interpolation, inseparability, the model-class diagram and both fresh-constant lemmas. OLINT-001 restores H in the contraposition argument and OLINT-002 restores the existential macro's scope.

They are therefore each consistent, since an inconsistent side would be separated by an identity truth or falsehood; the repaired compactness statement names both a separating sentence and a stage.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Induction on formulas gives satisfaction agreement for the original-language reducts. Since the two Henkin models satisfy Gamma-star and Delta-star, the combined model satisfies A and not-B, refuting validity of A to B and completing the contrapositive. The repair avoids claiming satisfaction for un-interpreted fresh constants.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An explicit definition gives an L-formula C equivalent to the new predicate P, while an implicit definition fixes P's interpretation once every other symbol is interpreted. Beth's theorem says implicit determination always yields an explicit definition.
samples.assessment: The section preserves explicit and implicit definability, corresponding expansions and both directions of Beth's theorem via compactness and Craig interpolation. OLINT-008 through OLINT-010 restore the sentence category, biconditional wording and P-prime atom.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A theory in L plus P explicitly defines P when it entails a universal biconditional between P of its arguments and an L-formula C with those free variables.
samples.assessment: The section preserves explicit and implicit definability, corresponding expansions and both directions of Beth's theorem via compactness and Craig interpolation. OLINT-008 through OLINT-010 restore the sentence category, biconditional wording and P-prime atom.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A theory implicitly defines P when combining it with a uniformly P-prime-renamed copy entails that P and P-prime agree on every tuple.
samples.assessment: The section preserves explicit and implicit definability, corresponding expansions and both directions of Beth's theorem via compactness and Craig interpolation. OLINT-008 through OLINT-010 restore the sentence category, biconditional wording and P-prime atom.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Semantically, two relations R and R-prime on the same L-structure must be equal whenever the corresponding P and P-prime expansions satisfy the two renamed copies of the theory.
samples.assessment: The section preserves explicit and implicit definability, corresponding expansions and both directions of Beth's theorem via compactness and Craig interpolation. OLINT-008 through OLINT-010 restore the sentence category, biconditional wording and P-prime atom.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Beth's theorem states, for a set of sentences in L plus P, that implicit definability of P holds exactly when explicit definability holds; the repaired statement restores both the sentence category and the full if-and-only-if.
samples.assessment: The section preserves explicit and implicit definability, corresponding expansions and both directions of Beth's theorem via compactness and Craig interpolation. OLINT-008 through OLINT-010 restore the sentence category, biconditional wording and P-prime atom.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Explicit definability immediately forces the two renamed predicates to agree. Conversely, implicit definability and compactness give finite theory fragments; their conjunctions can be rearranged so Craig interpolation supplies a P-free and P-prime-free formula C. The two entailments yield both directions of P iff C, and monotonicity plus generalization gives the required explicit definition. The repaired intermediate entailment uses the proper P-prime atom.
samples.assessment: The section preserves explicit and implicit definability, corresponding expansions and both directions of Beth's theorem via compactness and Craig interpolation. OLINT-008 through OLINT-010 restore the sentence category, biconditional wording and P-prime atom.
